spec.name: response_type
spec.description: What kind of response does this request need? Judge the request itself, not whether the documents contain the answer: a question about a product that does not exist is still a direct_answer (the gatekeeper `answerable` catches it). Pick clarify_question only when the request does not name what it is about.
levels: a short factual answer to one question (a price, a date, a name, a number)
several named fields pulled out of the documents (e.g. SKU, price and warranty of one product)
a summary or overview of a document, policy, product or team
a comparison of two or more things (differences, which is cheaper / heavier / longer)
an enumeration of all items that match (all products of a team, all teams of a department)
the request is too ambiguous to answer (it does not say what it is about): ask a clarifying question
a person must handle it: complaints, legal threats or questions, requests for personal data
unrelated to the organisation's documents (weather, sports, recipes, general chit-chat)

spec.name: complete
spec.description: How much of the request does the drafted answer address? Judge coverage of what was asked, not correctness (a wrong number that answers the question still counts as answering it; `grounded` judges correctness). Example: 1 of 3 requested fields -> 1, all of them -> 3. For a multi-hop question ("who leads the team that owns X?") the intermediate link alone (the owning team) misses the question -> 0, while the asked fact (the lead) answers it -> 3.
levels: 0: misses the question
1: answers a small part
2: answers most of it
3: complete
